title: Had it done: the causative passive
goal: Say what was had done or commissioned, and tell who ordered the work from who did it.

intro.text: Causative + passive is **had done**: *Ev boyatıldı* (Someone had the house painted). With *tarafından*, it names who ordered the work: *Cami Kanuni tarafından yaptırıldı* (commissioned by Süleyman), but *Sinan tarafından yapıldı* (built by Sinan). After a causative, the passive is always `-Il`.

exercises.question: *Süleymaniye Camii, Kanuni Sultan Süleyman tarafından yaptırıldı.* What was Süleyman's role?
options: He built it with his own hands.

why.1: That would be *yapıldı*, without the causative. *Yaptırıldı* means someone had it built.
why.2: The architect was Mimar Sinan: *Sinan tarafından yapıldı*.

exercises.explain: *yap-tır-ıl-dı*: with a causative passive, *tarafından* names the person who ordered the work.

exercises.en: The house was painted last year (we had it done).

reject.why: *Boyandı* is the plain passive, **was painted**. To say someone had it painted, the causative comes first: *boya-t-ıl-dı*.
*Boyattı* is active: **he had it painted**. The house is the subject, so add the passive: *boyatıldı*.

exercises.explain: *boya-t* (have painted) + *-ıl* (passive) + *-dı*: the house was painted, on someone's order.

exercises.label: *bekletilmek*, past: I was kept waiting, you were kept waiting…
exercises.explain: *bekle-t-il-*: the causative *-t* (after a vowel), then the passive *-il*. Front vowels throughout: *bekletildim*.
After voiceless p the causative is *-tır*; then the passive *-ıl*, the negative *-ma*, the past *-dı*.

exercises.prompt: We were kept waiting for an hour.

reject.why: *Bekledik* is **we waited**. **We were kept waiting** needs the causative and the passive: *bekle-t-il-di-k*.
*Beklendik* is **we were waited for**. **Kept waiting** is *bekletildik*.

exercises.explain: *bekle-t-il-di-k*: someone made us wait, and the passive leaves them unnamed.

accept: The mistakes were corrected in red pen.
The mistakes were corrected with red pen.
The mistakes were corrected with a red pen.
The errors were corrected in red pen.
The errors were corrected with red pen.
The errors were corrected with a red pen.
The [mistakes|errors] were corrected [in|with|with a] red pencil.

exercises.en: This fabric was embroidered by hand.

exercises.question: Which sentence names the person who did the work with their own hands?

why.1: *Yaptırıldı* names the person who ordered it, not the builder.
why.2: No one is named here at all.

exercises.explain: With a plain passive, *tarafından* is the doer: *Sinan tarafından yapıldı*.

exercises.text: The food was cooked over a wood fire.

exercises.prompt: The guests were shown the workshop.

reject.why: The people who see stay in the dative: *misafirlere*.
*Gösterdi* is **he showed**. **Were shown** is the passive: *göster-il-di*.

exercises.explain: *Göstermek* is a causative in form, so its passive is *-il*: *gösterildi*. The guests stay in the dative.

exercises.en: The carpets were sent to be washed last week.
These tiles were made by craftsmen from İznik.
exercises.explain: The craftsmen did the work themselves, so the plain passive: *yapıldı*. *Yaptırıldı* would make them the people who ordered the tiles.

exercises.task: Describe a well-known building in a city you know in three or four sentences: who had it built, who built it, when, and what was done to it later. Use at least one causative passive (`yaptırıldı`, `boyatıldı`…) and one plain passive.
models: Süleymaniye Camii 1550'lerde Kanuni Sultan Süleyman tarafından yaptırıldı. Cami Mimar Sinan tarafından yapıldı. Çinileri İznik'te üretildi. Cami birkaç kez onarıldı.
Montreal'deki Notre-Dame Bazilikası 1820'lerde bir rahip topluluğu tarafından yaptırıldı. Kilisenin planları bir İrlandalı mimar tarafından çizildi. İçi daha sonra yeniden boyatıldı.
checklist: The person who ordered the building with *tarafından yaptırıldı*
The architect or builder with a plain passive: *tarafından yapıldı*, *çizildi*
Names with an apostrophe before the suffix (*Montreal'deki*), institutions without one
